title: Elazar ben Chanokh
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned unfavorably in Mishnah Eduyot 5:6: he disparaged the washing of hands and was excommunicated; he died under the ban, and they placed a stone on his coffin. Hyman infers from the passage that he lived in the time of Akavya ben Mahalalel.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Torat Emet 357 digital Mishnah Eduyot 5:6 has Eliezer ben Chanokh, whereas Hyman’s heading has Elazar. Hyman’s inference about Akavya’s time is retained as his inference, without identifying the two differently named entries automatically.

The checked Mishnah Eduyot 5:6 has Eliezer ben Chanokh, whereas Hyman’s heading is Elazar. Rabbi Yehudah’s account distinguishes this man from Akavya and describes the hand-purity dispute and the stone placed on his coffin. Hyman’s inferred contemporaneity remains his inference; the differently named forms are not silently harmonized.
